title: Maintenance Advice: Press 2 Cone Hydraulic Fault

sections.heading: Check first
items: Check the hydraulic oil level in the tank and look for dirty filters.
Inspect all hoses and fittings for visible external leaks.
Watch the cone pressure gauge for swings or spikes while the press is running.
Compare the current pressure fluctuations against the normal levels recorded over the last 30 days.

sections.heading: Step by step
items: Stop the machine and release all stored hydraulic pressure.
Replace any leaking hoses and worn seals found during inspection.
Change the hydraulic filter to remove potential contamination.
Top up the system with the specific oil grade named in the manufacturer's manual.
Test the cone pressure under load to ensure the squeeze on the fruit is stable.
Record all findings and replaced parts in the work order.

sections.heading: Safety
items: Perform lock-out/tag-out: switch off, isolate electrical and hydraulic energy, lock, tag, and test that the machine cannot move.
Release all stored hydraulic pressure before opening any lines to prevent fluid injection injuries.
Ensure the work area is clean of oil spills to prevent slips.

sections.heading: Parts and tools
items: Two hydraulic hoses.
One seal kit.
One hydraulic filter.
Hydraulic oil grade as specified in the mill's SOP (Standard Operating Procedure).
Standard mechanical tools for hydraulic maintenance.

sections.heading: Call the manufacturer if
items: The pressure continues to hunt, which means the relief valve cannot maintain a steady setting.
The hydraulic pump shows signs of failure or cannot reach required pressure.
Internal leakage persists after all seals have been replaced.
Required torque values or clearances are not listed in the manual.
